title: Tait colouring of Hamiltonian cubic graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is $3$-regular, so every vertex has exactly three neighbours, and suppose $G$ admits a Hamiltonian cycle, a closed walk that visits every vertex exactly once. Then the line graph of $G$ — whose vertices are the edges of $G$, two being adjacent precisely when they share an endpoint — is $3$-colourable; equivalently, the edges of $G$ can be properly coloured with three colours, a Tait colouring.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
